title: Hush the Loud Cannon's Roar
description: Hush the Loud Cannon's Roar in Tonic Solfa to BOYLSTON, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: John Johns wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 184, “Human Brotherhood”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to BOYLSTON; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Hush the loud can-non's roar, The fran-tic war-rior's call! Why should the earth be drenched with gore? Are we not broth-ers all?

lines: Why should the earth be drenched with gore?
Sweet mercy, melt the oppressor's heart, —
Let love each harsher feeling drown, —
That heaven its work at length may own,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: John Johns died in 1847.
credits: Words by John Johns (1801–1847), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to BOYLSTON by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
